notes: Go rebuilt from beginner to professional for Go 1.27: 19 new lessons and a "Working like a pro" unit (modules, project layout, go vet, CI, slog, flags, shipping binaries)
New Go lessons on files with os.Root, time zones, iterators, json/v2, reflection, fuzzing, the race detector, pprof, cgo, embed and templates, and secure coding
Every Go exercise has tests proven to reject common wrong answers, and every lesson has a "Common mistakes" note

New course, early access: Roblox game development in Luau, with a simulated Roblox engine so scripts run right in the app (units 1 and 2: the Luau language, then parts, events, players, leaderstats, timers and tags)

New course: Logic from beginner to pro, made to be easy to follow — true and false, if/then, sets, arguments and fallacies, proof, and the logic inside a CPU, finishing with a truth-table generator, a tiny SAT solver and a logic-gate simulator

New course: OSINT (open-source intelligence), taught ethics-first on simulated data only — searching, geolocation, infrastructure and metadata, footprints and verification — with strong lawful-use and consent guidance and a privacy-redaction capstone

New course: Ethical hacking tools, taught lawfully and defensively — authorisation and the law, reconnaissance, traffic and the web, credentials and hashing, defence (blue team) and reporting — where every exercise runs on bundled simulated data and never touches a real system
A new "Security & investigation" category for the Logic, OSINT and ethical-hacking courses, whose exercises are all verified to reject common wrong answers
Lesson examples now run with their sample input and files when you press Run in the lesson
